glossary.m: the big lesson a story teaches, said as a full sentence
a person who checks writing and fixes capitals, punctuation and spelling
the name of one particular person, place or thing, like Lucy or Cair Paravel. It starts with a capital.
a part of a word with one vowel sound. Garden has two: gar and den.
the main part of a word that holds its meaning, like port, which means carry
a comparison that uses like or as
telling the truth, even when it is hard

cards.title: World Notes: The White Stag
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read with your lens in mind.
text: In old legends from Europe, a white stag or white deer is very hard to catch. When hunters chase one, it often leads them into a great adventure.
Some stories about King Arthur begin with a white stag running through the forest.
Real white deer do exist, but they are very rare. In Chapter 17, the White Stag leads the four rulers back to the lamp-post.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. This is the last day with the book. Explain it in your own words, and finish your response.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: roll root words, fix a passage in passes, and split words by syllable.
transcripts.guide2: Look back through the whole book for your best proof.
transcripts.guide3: Today you publish your literary response.

notes.wordParts: Roots from this year: inter = between, trans = across, form = shape, ject = throw, script and scribe = write, port = carry, struct = build.
notes.grammar: An editor checks in passes. Capitals for names and the first word. Apostrophes for belonging and joined words. A comma before and or but when it joins two complete thoughts.
notes.spelling: Syllable types: closed (cat), open (go), silent-e (bake), vowel team (rain), r-controlled (car), consonant-le (table).
notes.wgrd: A good theme statement works for the whole book: the beginning, the middle and the end. The ending is the strongest proof.
vocab: the supreme ruler of a country or kingdom
the ceremony in which a ruler is officially crowned
restored to friendship or peace after a conflict

plate.alt: A painting on gold of a white deer lying in green grass, with a gold crown around its neck and a gold chain
plate.credit: The Wilton Diptych, outer panel (the white hart) · unknown artist, about 1395–1399 · National Gallery, London · Public domain
plate.look: This white deer was painted more than 600 years ago for King Richard II of England. A hart is an old word for a stag, and the white hart was the king’s own sign. Look at the gold crown around its neck. In Chapter 17, the kings and queens ride out to hunt the White Stag.
plate.lookBtn: Tap to learn about this painting of a white deer

mods.todo: Listen to Opti. Then tap the lens you will use today.
mods.script: [warmly] Here's today's reading tip. A strong theme fits the beginning, the middle and the end of a book. Test yours one last time. Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one first. The Magician's Nephew was written by C.S. Lewis, and it tells how Narnia began. The important words in a book title get capitals. C.S. has a capital and a period for each letter. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Find a metaphor, a personification and a hyperbole. Say each one out loud.

mods.todo: Say what one root means. Roll the dice. Say what each word means, then check.
mods.script: Quick question: what does trans mean? Across! Here's a word that's not on the dice. Transatlantic. It means across the Atlantic Ocean, like a ship sailing from England to America. Say what the word part means. Then tap Roll the Dice. Say what the word means, and tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six words.

mods.todo: Choose one word. Write one sentence about the ending and the theme.
mods.script: Watch me use a word about the whole book. Reconciled. In the end, Edmund and his family are reconciled. One word, the whole story. Now choose your word, and write your own sentence about the ending.

mods.todo: Fix it in passes. Then tap all five words that need fixing.
mods.script: Two passes, like an editor. the professors house was big and the children explored it. Pass one, capitals: The, and Professor, because it's his name. Pass two, apostrophes and commas: Professor's, and a comma before and. Now do your passes, and tap every word that needs fixing.

mods.todo: Roll the dice. Split the word and name its syllable types. Then check.
mods.script: Dice roll: pilot! Split it after the vowel: pi, lot. Pi is open, so the i says its name. Lot is closed. Tap Roll the dice, split the word, name its syllable types, and tap Check my answer.

mods.todo: Look back through the whole book. Then try the Truth Watch below.
mods.script: No new chapters today. This is your last day with the book. Look back for your strongest proof from the beginning, the middle and the end. Then try the Truth Watch and the three questions.

mods.todo: Answer each question in full sentences. Use details from the book.
mods.script: Three questions to finish the book, in full sentences. One, your best theme statement. Two, the moment that mattered most to you. Three, why readers still love this book.

mods.todo: Write your finished response: title, theme, proof from three chapters, closing.
mods.script: Last step: publish. Clara read hers out loud one more time and changed one last word. Read yours, fix one thing, and write your finished response.

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: In Chapter 5, the Professor asks who is more truthful, Lucy or Edmund, and Peter says, up till now, Lucy every time.
items.why: Peter is fair to Lucy, even though he doubts her story.

items.t: Lucy tells the others about Narnia the very first time, even though they laugh.
In Chapter 12, Peter tells Aslan that his own anger helped Edmund go wrong.
items.why: He owns his part, instead of blaming only Edmund.
